covers.quote: Use passive voice only if there is a good reason – for example, if you can’t say who did the action or because information has to be concealed for ethical or legal reasons.

examples.note: Active voice example following subject-verb-object order.

parts.quote: Computer models produce wind forecasts to show average speeds.

examples.note: Permitted use of passive voice where the actor is unknown or concealed for confidentiality/ethical reasons.

parts.quote: A formal complaint was made about the use of discriminatory language.

rules.quote: Build most sentences in this order with active voice when using active verbs (doing or action verbs).
rules.specification: Use the active voice (subject–verb–object order) for most sentences, reserving the passive voice for situations where the agent cannot be identified or must be concealed for ethical or legal reasons.
rules.violation_condition: a sentence written in the passive voice without a specific justification
when: When using active (doing or action) verbs.
Passive voice is permitted when you cannot say who did the action.
Passive voice is permitted when information has to be concealed for ethical or legal reasons.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: 'Use passive voice only if there is a good reason' states exceptions/conditions for when passive voice is permissible, consolidated under the core active voice rule.
